question: When did the United Nations declare the World Physics Year, also known as the Einstein Year, to mark the 100th anniversary of the physicist Albert Einstein?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2005**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** United Nations has declared 2005 to be the International Year of Physics**. This declaration coincides with the 100th anniversary of physicist **Albert Einstein's "miraculous year".**
 
• **Three of Einstein's most well-known scientific articles were written in 1905: the theory of relativity, quantum theory and the theory of Brownian motion.**
 
• 2005 was declared the **World Year of Physics** by the International Union of Pure and Applied Physics, following a proposal from the **World Congress of Physical Societies** and a resolution by the World Congress of Physical Societies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Albert Einstein**

 
 
• Albert Einstein was a theoretical physicist born in Germany and one of the best and most influential physicists of all time**.**
 
• His discovery of the **law of the photoelectric effect**, a crucial milestone in the development of **quantum theory**, earned him the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics.
 
• One of the man-made elements in the periodic table, **Einsteinium**, bears his name.
